next_steps: Jordan to send benchmark plan + golden prompts (by 2026-04-22)

summary: POC scoping focused on quality evaluation plan for clinical summarization and triage use cases. Agreed to a light 2-week pilot comparing Redwood hosted vs dedicated config using golden prompts, hallucination checks, format checks, and automated scoring. Key success criteria: >= 90% precision on key-entities, <2% hallucination rate on clinical facts, average generation latency <700ms at 95th percentile, and acceptable cost per 1k tokens. Next steps include sharing golden prompts, infra checklist, and sample workloads.
topics: Quality eval plan: golden prompts, regression tests, hallucination/format checks
questions: How do we define hallucination failures for clinical notes?
What are acceptable latency SLOs for triage vs summarization?
Can Redwood run evaluation on-prem or do we need de-id samples?
What telemetry and logs will be available during pilot?
transcript:
00:00 Jordan Kim: ok hey everybody uh thanks for joining from Redwood, i'm Jordan (AE), and Priya our solutions engineer is also on. How's everyone doing?
00:07 Lisa Monroe: hey Jordan, hey Priya, good, thanks. we have a short agenda — we want to scope the poc for our clinical summarization and triage flows.
00:14 Priya Shah: great — we'll focus on quality evaluation plan, workload sizing, and benchmarks, and then align on timelines. does that sound right lisa?
00:20 Lisa Monroe: yes perfect. quick intro — i'm lisa, head of AI at HarborCare; carlos here owns data pipelines; erin owns clinical requirements.
00:26 Carlos Diaz: yep thanks, hi.
00:28 Erin Patel: hello.
00:32 Jordan Kim: cool quick q to start — what are your primary success criteria for the poc? is it accuracy, latency, cost, or some combo?
00:40 Lisa Monroe: primarily accuracy on entity extraction and factuality, we need high precision on med names, dosages, and problem lists. latency matters for triage — ideally sub-second, 95th percentile under a second, but for batch summarization we can tolerate higher. cost is secondary but still a consideration.
00:58 Priya Shah: ok so we should capture two buckets: triage (low-latency, high-throughput) and summarization (higher quality, can be slightly slower). For quality evals, our plan is golden prompts + regression tests + hallucination checks + format validation. we'll propose scoring thresholds.
01:14 Lisa Monroe: can you expand on the golden prompts and regression tests? what exactly will you need from us?
01:20 Priya Shah: sure — golden prompts are a curated set of representative inputs with gold-standard outputs so we can measure exact-match, F1 on entities, and structural conformity. regression tests are an automated harness that runs the prompts on model variants and flags drops in metrics compared to a baseline. we'll also include hallucination detectors — for clinical facts we'll check whether generated assertions are supported by input or known-safe sources; when in doubt we mark as hallucination.
01:44 Erin Patel: how do you handle partial matches? e.g., med names with different tokenization or synonyms?
01:50 Priya Shah: we use normalized entity matching (stemming, canonical mapping for drug names), plus fuzzy matching thresholds. we'll report both strict and relaxed scores so you can decide the cutoffs.
02:01 Carlos Diaz: what about format checks — we have strict JSON schema for outputs, we can't accept free-form.
02:06 Jordan Kim: yes we can enforce schema validation as part of the pipeline — failures count as test failures. we'll include sample schema and validators.
02:12 Lisa Monroe: great. what about hallucination definition for ingestion of external notes — sometimes model infers things not in the note but plausible; we need zero tolerance for new clinical assertions.
02:24 Priya Shah: understood — for the poc we'll treat any assertion about a patient that is not explicitly present in the source note or in structured fields as a hallucination. we'll create a checklist of claim types to flag.
02:35 Jordan Kim: next let's talk workload sizing — carlos, can you share expected qps, avg tokens, and peak windows?
02:42 Carlos Diaz: for triage: typically 250 TPS at peak across our system, but the service-side calls will be fewer — we expect 50 concurrent infer requests to start, avg prompt size maybe 600 tokens, response about 400 tokens. summarization job runs in batch — 5k docs per hour during peak.
03:04 Priya Shah: ok that helps. for benchmarks we'll run two configs: 1) Redwood hosted (multi-tenant) and 2) Redwood dedicated reserved capacity with GPU quantization. we'll run the same golden prompts and measure latency p50/p95, cost per 1k tokens, entity F1, hallucination rate, and schema pass rate.
03:23 Lisa Monroe: timing — how long for the pilot?
03:26 Jordan Kim: suggested minimal pilot is 2 weeks: first week onboarding + initial runs, second week focused benchmarking and tuning. total 10 business days. does that fit your timeline?
03:35 Lisa Monroe: yes we want results before our vendor decision meeting on May 5th, so 2-week pilot starting around Apr 27th works.
03:42 Erin Patel: security — we require SOC2, SSO (SAML), KMS integration, and audit logs. how does Redwood handle key management?
03:50 Priya Shah: we support customer-managed keys via KMS/HSM integrations; i will send the infra checklist for VPC peering, subnet requirements, and KMS setup. audit logs and per-request tracing are available via the console and can be exported to your SIEM.
04:05 Carlos Diaz: for the sample data — can you de-id or do we need to de-id before sharing?
04:09 Priya Shah: Redwood is flexible; for hosted we require de-id or synthetic anonymized samples. if you want to run private deployment we can support secure data paths but that takes longer. for the quick pilot de-id is simplest.
04:20 Lisa Monroe: ok we'll de-id and share a 2-week sample set by Apr 27th.
04:25 Jordan Kim: scoring approach — we'll produce a combined score: weighted sum of entity F1 (40%), hallucination penalty (30%), schema pass rate (20%), latency penalty (10%). Thresholds to pass the poc: combined score > 0.85, hallucination rate < 2% for clinical assertions, and p95 latency < 700ms for triage.
04:46 Erin Patel: can you show sample reports?
04:48 Priya Shah: yes example report: for each prompt we show input, expected output, model output, entity diff, hallucination flags (binary), schema pass/fail, latency, and cost. we'll include aggregated dashboards.
04:59 Lisa Monroe: what about regression frequency? we want nightly runs when models are updated.
05:03 Priya Shah: agreed — regression harness will be scheduled nightly for the pilot and will produce alerts for metric regressions beyond configured deltas.
05:12 Jordan Kim: any concerns on the customer side about vendor lock-in or model variants?
05:16 Carlos Diaz: we need the ability to pin model versions and see performance across quantized variants.
05:20 Priya Shah: absolutely — the platform supports version pinning and automatic fallback to compatible variants if primary is congested. we'll include model catalog details.
05:30 Lisa Monroe: competitors — we've looked at Anthropic and Vertex; main difference for us is observability and throughput.
05:36 Jordan Kim: understood — our bench plan will emphasize traceability and per-token cost breakdown so you can compare apples-to-apples.
05:44 Erin Patel: can you confirm the definition of hallucination test? is it automated or manual adjudication?
05:49 Priya Shah: automated checks will catch many issues (unsupported claims, invented diagnoses), but for nuanced clinical claims we'll have a human review sample set — we'll do spot-check adjudication for borderline cases.
06:02 Lisa Monroe: ok good. next steps recap?
06:05 Jordan Kim: i'll recap: jordan to send benchmark plan + pricing; priya to send infra checklist and golden prompt template; harborcare to share de-id sample data and success criteria doc; schedule SE deep dive week of Apr 27.
06:18 Lisa Monroe: yes and action items noted. thanks everyone.
06:22 Jordan Kim: thanks all, we'll follow up via email and post the SOW draft. bye.
45:00 (call end)
